extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in geometric analysis / mathematicians studying Ricci flow and 3-manifold topology
extracted.subtask_description: Precise a priori assumptions, definitions and quantitative criteria used to construct and control Ricci flow solutions with surgery on compact orientable three-manifolds (Perelman-style). Includes canonical neighborhood classification, pinching/derivative estimates, noncollapsing/volume conditions, and surgery fineness conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pinching assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The eigenvalues λ ≥ µ ≥ ν of the curvature operator of the solution to the Ricci flow with surgery at each point and each time satisfy a pinching inequality controlling negative curvature (stated as (7.3.3) in the text) whenever ν < 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pinching relation must hold at every point/time for surgically modified solutions; it is used to ensure nonnegativity-type control and to guarantee that limits of rescaled solutions have nonnegative sectional curvature. The initial metric is normalized to help ensure the pinching estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy ε)
rubrics_metrics.description: For given ε>0 there exist constants C1,C2 and a nonincreasing positive function r(t) such that at each time t>0 every point x with scalar curvature R(x,t) ≥ r(t)^{-2} has a neighborhood B = Bt(x,σ) (for some 0<σ<C1 R(x,t)^{-1/2}) which is one of: (a) a strong ε-neck (slice of parabolic neighborhood ε-close to the evolving round cylinder after scaling), (b) an ε-cap, or (c) a compact manifold (without boundary) of positive sectional curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally the scalar curvature in B is between C1^{-1}R(x,t) and C2 R(x,t), gradient estimates |∇R|<η R^{3/2}, |∂R/∂t|<η R^2 hold in B, and there is a volume upper bound for cases (a) and (b). The definition allows r to depend on time and includes a volume upper bound to control sizes of canonical neighborhoods. These conditions are imposed with accuracy ε and constants depend only on ε.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of ε-neck (radius r)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ε-neck of radius r is an open set diffeomorphic to S^2×I that, after scaling by r^{-2}, is C^{[ε^{-1}]} ε-close to the corresponding subset of the standard round cylinder S^2×I (with S^2 of scalar curvature 1 and I of length 2ε^{-1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closeness is in the high (C^{[ε^{-1}]}) topology and includes geometry of the product metric; strong ε-neck is the time-slice of a parabolic neighborhood that is ε-close to the evolving round cylinder after parabolic rescaling and time shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: ε-tube, ε-horn, double ε-horn
rubrics_metrics.description: A metric on S^2×I is an ε-tube, ε-horn, or double ε-horn if each point is contained in some ε-neck and the scalar curvature behavior on the two ends is: bounded on both ends (ε-tube), bounded on one end and tends to infinity on the other (ε-horn), or tends to infinity on both ends (double ε-horn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are used to classify ends of regions with neck-like geometry; they control how one locates surgery necks and caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: ε-cap and capped ε-horn
rubrics_metrics.description: An ε-cap is a metric on B^3 or RP^3  ar{B}^3 such that the complement of a suitable compact subset is an ε-neck. A capped ε-horn is a metric on B^3 or RP^3  ar{B}^3 where outside some compact subset each point is contained in an ε-neck and scalar curvature tends to infinity on the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps are the standard pieces glued in during surgery to replace removed horn-ends; capped ε-horns model regions that are end-compactified by adding caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative estimates for high curvature points (gradient estimates)
rubrics_metrics.description: At points with R(x,t) ≥ r0^{-2} (for appropriate r0) universal estimates hold: |∇R| < η R^{3/2} and |∂R/∂t| < η R^2, where η>0 is a universal constant (see (7.3.1) and (7.3.4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These local derivative bounds are required in canonical neighborhoods and are used to pass to smooth limits and control evolution near high curvature regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: κ-noncollapsed (Perelman's no local collapsing theorem II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given parameters (e.g. A), there exists κ=κ(A)>0 such that any complete solution satisfying the stated geometric assumptions is κ-noncollapsed on scales r0 over the specified region (i.e., volume lower bounds relative to curvature scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncollapsing is independent of small parameters like α and is used repeatedly to extract geometric limits and to guarantee canonical neighborhood volume lower bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical neighborhood classification for very high curvature points
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rescaled scalar curvature at a point exceeds a large threshold K, then (after appropriate normalization) that point has a canonical neighborhood which is either a (2ε)-neck, a (2ε)-cap, or a compact manifold diffeomorphic to a metric quotient of the round three-sphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This classification is used to identify regions where surgery may be needed and to show subsequential rescaled limits are ancient κ-solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curvature control via volume growth at a time slice (Theorem 7.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any w>0 there exist τ(w)>0, α(w)>0, K(w) such that: if on a ball B_{t0}(x0,r0) at time t0 (with r0<α) one has Rm(x,t0) ≥ - r0^{-2} and Vol_{t0}(B_{t0}(x0,r0)) ≥ w r0^3, then for times t ∈ [t0 - τ r0^2, t0] and points with d_t(x,x0) ≤ τ r0, the scalar curvature satisfies R(x,t) ≤ K r0^{-2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces lower curvature bounds on an entire time interval by a lower bound at a single time slice together with a volume lower bound, yielding forward curvature control on a backward-in-time parabolic neighborhood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localized curvature bound with spatial radius parameter A (Corollary 7.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given w>0 and A<∞ there are τ(w,A), K(w,A), α(w,A) so that under the same hypotheses as Theorem 7.2.2 on B_{t0}(x0,r0) (r0<α) one obtains R(x,t) ≤ K r0^{-2} for t ∈ [t0 - τ r0^2, t0] for all x with d_t(x,x0) ≤ A r0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives curvature control on a larger spatial region (distance ≤ A r0) under the same volume+lower bound hypotheses, useful when one needs estimates on a fixed multiple of the ball radius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of fine surgery necks in ε-horns (Lemma 7.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given small ε, δ (<ε) and T, there exists a radius h (0<h<δ ρ, depending only on δ and r(T)) such that if x is a point in an ε-horn of (Ω, �g) with boundary in Ω_ρ and h(x)=�R(x)^{-1/2}≤h, then the parabolic neighborhood B_T(x, δ^{-1} h(x))×[T- h(x)^2, T] is, after scaling by h(x)^{-2}, δ-close to the corresponding subset of the evolving standard round cylinder (i.e., a strong δ-neck).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the quantitative guarantee that in every ε-horn one can find 'fine' (arbitrarily close) necks at a controlled small scale h; these are the necks where one may perform surgery without losing the a priori assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Ricci flow with surgery (surgically modified solution)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Ricci flow with surgery is a (finite or countable) collection of smooth Ricci flow solutions g_k(t) defined on compact orientable manifolds M_k for time intervals [t^-_k, t^+_k] such that the forward limit (Ω_k, �g_k) at t^+_k and the backward limit at t^-_{k+1} contain compact isometric submanifolds which are identified; the union of the intervals is the overall time interval and the t^+_k are the surgery times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an abstract definition: surgery is implemented by cutting along isometric submanifolds (usually necks) and gluing caps, producing subsequent smooth flows. The definition encodes the continuity of topology through identified isometric pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgery strategy: only perform surgeries on ε-horns using fine necks
rubrics_metrics.description: Surgery is performed in ε-horns (not arbitrary ε-necks or ε-caps) at sufficiently fine necks (as in Lemma 7.3.2) to avoid accumulation of surgery errors; tubes and caps are not generally cut since fine necks may not exist there and rough surgeries could cause loss of control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The restriction to ε-horns with fine necks is motivated by the need to preserve the a priori assumptions uniformly through successive surgeries and to prevent error accumulation that could destroy the recognizability of high curvature regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite-ness/compactness criteria for Ω_ρ
rubrics_metrics.description: For Ω the set where curvature stays bounded as t→T and Ω_ρ = {x∈Ω : �R(x) ≤ ρ^{-2}} (for ρ<r0), Ω_ρ is compact; components of Ω containing points of Ω_ρ are finitely many and each such component has finitely many ends (each an ε-horn). Components containing no points of Ω_ρ are capped ε-horns or double ε-horns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These structural/compactness facts are used to decide where to cut and cap at the singular time and to reconstruct the topology of the initial manifold by truncating horns and gluing caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization of initial metric
rubrics_metrics.description: By scaling the initial Riemannian metric one may assume it is normalized; normalization is used to guarantee the pinching estimates and to start the induction/construction of the long-time surgically modified solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization simplifies constants in estimates and is a standard preparatory step; the subsequent a priori assumptions and constants are given relative to the normalized initial data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two main difficulties to resolve for surgery procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When constructing Ricci flow with surgery one must (i) prevent surgery times from accumulating, and (ii) obtain long-time behavior of the surgically modified solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All the a priori assumptions, fineness lemmas, and curvature/volume controls are directed to resolve these two issues by producing uniform controls that persist through surgeries.
